sentences.text: The case originated from Crime No.1282 of 2011 registered at the Thrissur Town East Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 4, 5 and 6 of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978 and was subsequently entrusted with the CBCID.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The prosecution allegation is that the 4 th accused, in his capacity as Managing Director and accused Nos.5 to 13, as Directors of A1 to A3 companies conducted promotional business meets at various places and influenced people through brochures, advertisements etc. and deceived persons into investing money in the business plan of the accused by promising to pay high profits as returns and huge amounts as commission for enrolling new members.
It is alleged that the accused companies failed to provide the promised benefit to the depositors and thereby committed the alleged offences.

Contending that he was not a Director of the accused companies at the relevant point of time, 2025:KER:10455 CRL.MC NO. 1239 OF 2025 petitioner moved an application for discharge which the learned Magistrate rejected as per Annexure C order.
Aggrieved, the petitioner filed revision before the Sessions Court and the same was dismissed as per Annexure D order.
This Criminal M.C. is filed seeking to quash Annexure D order.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner was the Director of the 3 rd accused company only for the period from 13.05.2010 to 26.07.2010 and the company had given information regarding commencement of its business by submitting an application in Form No.20 only on 14.06.2010.
As such, the petitioner was the Director of the 3 rd accused company only for a few days.
The prosecution does not have a case that any business activity of the 3rd accused company had taken place during those days.
Moreover, the petitioner cannot be mulcted with criminal liability, unless it is shown that he was responsible for the functioning or the conduct of business of the company.
It is argued that the Sessions Court rejected the revision filed by the petitioner without considering the contentions on merits.
4. I heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.

5. There is substantial merit in the contention of the 2025:KER:10455 CRL.MC NO. 1239 OF 2025 learned counsel for the petitioner that, except an omnibus statement in paragraph 7 of the impugned order that the period between 13.05.2010 and 26.07.2010, when the petitioner was a Director of the 3rd accused company, is the relevant period, the finding itself is rendered without reference to any reliable material.
This aspect assumes relevance in the light of the specific contention of the petitioner that, even the bank account of the company was opened one month after his resignation.
Moreover, this Court, as per Annexures A and B orders, had directed the court below to consider all relevant aspects while deciding the application for discharge.
The court below having failed to do so, the impugned order is liable to be interfered with.
In the result, the Crl.M.C. is allowed.
Annexure D order is quashed and the Additonal Sessions Court-IV, Thrissur is directed to reconsider the revision petition afresh and pass a reasoned order thereon, as expeditiously as possible.
